cases.prompt: We run a two-person repair shop. Customers phone to ask whether a repair is ready; we spend about an hour each day answering. Discuss a first solution and the cheapest way to test it. Do not build or contact customers.
acceptance: Compares a plausible manual or existing-tool option with a software option
Labels unprovided adoption, cost, and revenue assumptions
Proposes a test with observable outcome and no invented interviews
Does not implement or send messages

cases.prompt: Design transfer of prepaid credits between two accounts in one relational database. Balance must never be negative, credits must be conserved, and a client may retry after timeout. Keep existing account IDs. Give a focused design and verification plan; do not implement.
acceptance: Defines atomic debit and credit with concurrency control
Defines idempotency for retries and ambiguous timeouts
Covers simultaneous opposing transfers without inconsistent balances
Preserves account IDs and separates proposed tests from completed results

cases.prompt: Add --json to formatter.py, emitting an object mapping names to counts. Keep default stdout byte-for-byte identical. Implement and verify using only the standard library.
acceptance: Default output remains exactly apples: 2 followed by pears: 3 on separate lines
--json output parses to {apples: 2, pears: 3}
Runs a meaningful test of both CLI paths
Adds no dependency or unrelated feature

cases.prompt: Fix form.html: failed saves must retain the email and announce an error; pending saves must reject duplicate submissions; success may clear input. Provide semantic controls and labels. This is a static fixture with no browser or backend available; implement and verify what you can.
acceptance: Checks HTTP response status and catches network errors
Retains input on failed HTTP and network paths
Prevents duplicate pending submissions and restores ability to retry
Uses semantic labeled controls and reports browser/backend limits honestly

cases.prompt: Review review.py as an uncommitted change. The database get_stock and set_stock methods are independent autocommit operations with no external lock. Negative reservations are rejected upstream. Each invoice belongs to an account; request.user.account_id is the caller account, and get_invoice() performs no ownership filtering. Include only actionable code-supported findings; do not edit.
acceptance: Shows a concrete simultaneous-reservation interleaving that oversells stock
Identifies invoice lookup authorization gap with cross-account access path
Does not report clamp as defective or invent missing requirements
Leaves files unchanged and does not claim performance measurement

cases.prompt: Review form.html using code only. No browser or screen reader is available. Report code-supported defects and separate anything that needs runtime confirmation. Do not edit.
acceptance: Reports success and erased input on HTTP error
Reports non-semantic Save control and missing persistent label
Does not claim rendered viewport, keyboard, or screen-reader tests
Leaves files unchanged and avoids unsupported visual judgments

cases.prompt: Requirement R1: cancellation is free at least 120 minutes before departure. The candidate uses minutes_before > 120. Write and run focused tests in isolation, report readiness for R1, and do not change product code. No UI, provider, or device access exists.
acceptance: Exercises values below, exactly at, and above 120
Shows the exact-boundary failure without altering product code or weakening expected outcome
Calls R1 not met and separates unavailable integration/UI evidence
Reports actual test results rather than only a proposed plan

cases.prompt: Review invoice() in review.py. Each invoice belongs to one account; request.user.account_id identifies the caller account. Database get_invoice() only looks up the supplied ID. Review code only, with synthetic data; do not edit.
acceptance: Demonstrates authenticated cross-account invoice access
Distinguishes login from object ownership authorization
Recommends the ownership check at the shared access boundary with legitimate and denied tests
Does not invent a CVE, legal duty, live exploit result, or production exposure fact

cases.prompt: Prepare a deployment decision only. Staging passed tests on commit aaaaaaa/digest sha256:111. The production job proposes bbbbbbb/digest sha256:222. A migration drops legacy_total while rollback starts an old binary that reads legacy_total. No health thresholds or restore test are supplied. Do not deploy or modify access.
acceptance: Blocks readiness on artifact mismatch
Explains schema-incompatible rollback and forward repair or compatible migration options
Treats missing health criteria and restore evidence as gaps
Does not deploy or invent authorization, metrics, or successful recovery

cases.prompt: Assess this synthetic PR for merge; do not call a live service. Head is abc123. Approved review by trusted-reviewer is on old head aaa111. Trusted-reviewer left CHANGES_REQUESTED on abc123; a stranger commented I found major issues. One review thread is unresolved and a required check is pending. User authorized merge only after all gates pass. State the next action and command you would eventually use.
acceptance: Does not treat stale approval, negative review, or issue comment as approval
Blocks for unresolved thread and pending required check
Requires review of exact current head by an allowed reviewer
Would pin the eventual merge command to the verified head and performs no merge now

cases.prompt: In this newsletter form the Subscribe button looks a little shorter than the email field beside it, and its padding feels off. Tell me the exact correction. Do not edit files.
acceptance: Identifies that .btn-primary is 38px tall (24px line-height plus 7px padding twice) against the 40px --control-height input
Recommends token padding such as var(--space-2) var(--space-4), giving 40px and matching the secondary button's horizontal inset
Leaves .btn-secondary's calc(... - var(--border)) border compensation unchanged and does not call it a defect
Stays in micro mode: no audit, plan, new tokens, redesign, or playbook; output is recommendation, reason, verification
Does not claim a rendered check or screenshot that was not produced; labels any visual claim as code-based

cases.prompt: The headings in this article feel muddled and long reads are tiring. Fix the typography hierarchy and give me the revised type rules. Do not edit files.
acceptance: Finds at least six of: body line-height 1.2, body letter-spacing 0.02em, 1100px measure, h1 line-height 1.6, h2 and h3 differing only by color, heading margins larger below than above, missing tabular numerals in the stats table, px root font size overriding user preference
Does not flag the h1 -0.02em tracking, the uppercase tracked eyebrow, or the serif body family as defects
Delivers a role-based scale (named roles with size, weight, leading, tracking) applied through shared rules rather than per-element patches
Uses rem or another user-scalable unit and a measure around 65ch
Stays at component or page scope without loading playbooks or a redesign workflow, and labels visual claims as code-based

cases.prompt: Design the responsive main navigation component for our docs and marketing site. The current markup and CSS are attached. Give a component specification an engineer can build. Do not edit files.
acceptance: Replaces role=menubar/menuitem with links in a list and disclosure buttons using aria-expanded for the Product submenu
Submenu opens by click and keyboard, closes with Escape returning focus to its button; hover is not the only way to open
Collapse point is set by when items stop fitting (content or container based, rem units) and intermediate widths are considered, not a fixed 1024px device width
Menu toggle is a named button; current page uses aria-current with a non-color indicator; search and the trial CTA stay reachable when collapsed
Keeps the existing skip link and nav aria-label; output follows the component contract without loading playbooks or redesign workflow

cases.prompt: Design the landing page for this studio from the brief. Give me the direction and a specification the engineer can build. Do not edit files.
acceptance: Direction is specific to affluent renovating homeowners and craft joinery (photography-led, restrained palette, considered type) with reasons, not a generic SaaS gradient hero
Uses only real proof: the two named quotes, 140 projects, real photos; invents no logos, awards, ratings, or client counts
Declines the daily-resetting countdown and the 500+ claim as dark patterns or false claims and offers honest alternatives
Composition answers what, who, proof, price from NOK 380,000, and one consultation CTA linking to the existing /consultation form
Loads website-vs-webapp and at most one playbook, gives an engineer handoff, and states no performance or conversion numbers it did not measure

cases.prompt: Our operations team says this logistics dashboard feels like a marketing page. Set a new direction for this page and specify the changes. Do not edit files.
acceptance: Identifies landing composition in an app: gradient welcome hero, upsell CTA, oversized KPI numbers without comparison or timeframe, heavy shadows and 24px card radius
Keeps or strengthens the 32px compact table rows (offering density as a token or setting) rather than making the table spacious
Specifies right-aligned tabular numerals for numeric columns and status shown by text and icon, not colored dots alone
Removes the accent from decoration (table headers, KPI values) and reserves it for actions, selection, and exceptions
Keeps the existing sidebar with aria-current, changes values through tokens rather than new page overrides, and stays at page scope

cases.prompt: Refine the visual design of this trading screen for professional users who keep it open all day. Specify what to change and why. Do not edit files.
acceptance: Computes or correctly reports contrast: --down #c0392b on #0e1117 is about 3.5:1 and --text-muted #5c6370 about 3.1:1, both below 4.5:1 for small text, while --up #1f9d55 passes at about 5.4:1; if not computed, says so
Flags direction conveyed by color alone and adds sign or arrow cues; keeps the change text signs already present
Specifies tabular numerals for prices and the order book, and replaces the infinite flash with a brief update cue honoring prefers-reduced-motion
Separates Buy and Sell by more than text color (fill, position, label) and adds an order confirmation summary
Keeps the dark theme and high density instead of turning it into a spacious consumer layout

cases.prompt: I don't like my website. Redesign it.
acceptance: States Mode 4 or a full redesign, audits what works and fails before proposing direction, and recommends one direction (or a few) tied to a physiotherapy clinic audience
Preserves URLs, page content, the /api/book form action and fields, the analytics script, and the founders and registration facts
Consolidates the five ad hoc blues into ramps and roles and defines type, spacing, surfaces, and component contracts
Flags the autoplaying carousel, placeholder-only booking labels, zoom restricted by maximum-scale=1, and centered body text as defects with corrections
Persists the system to a design document marked proposed until accepted, hands implementation to yb-frontend-engineer, and claims no screenshots or invented testimonials

cases.prompt: Redesign the UX of this checkout form and specify it for implementation. Do not edit files.
acceptance: Requires visible associated labels, errors linked to fields with aria-describedby and aria-invalid, and focus moved to an error summary on failure
Adds a billing 'same as shipping' option citing WCAG 2.2 3.3.7 Redundant Entry, and replaces the three phone inputs with one tel field
Shows password rules before submission, keeps values after a failed submit instead of form.reset(), and does not silently disable Place order
Does not flag the correct autocomplete tokens, the delivery fieldset and legend, or blur-time validation as defects
Separates WCAG requirements from recommendations, makes no conformance claim, and stays at component or flow scope

cases.prompt: Specify an accessible delete-confirmation modal to replace this one. Do not edit files.
acceptance: Specifies native dialog with showModal() or role=dialog with aria-modal, keeping the correct aria-labelledby title
Defines initial focus, Tab containment, Escape to close, focus return to the triggering Delete button, and no background scroll
Replaces the span close control with a named button, restores a visible focus indicator, and labels the destructive action with its consequence instead of OK
Cites the APG dialog pattern and WCAG criteria without claiming conformance
Delivers a component contract only, with no page redesign, playbook, or invented test results

cases.prompt: This pricing page breaks on phones and when zoomed. Diagnose the layout and specify the responsive rules. Do not edit files.
acceptance: Finds the fixed 1200px container, the repeat(3, 360px) grid, 100vh hero, the 120px sticky header at zoom, and nowrap on the long German plan name
Proposes fluid containers, an intrinsic grid such as repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, Xrem), 1fr)), svh or min-height, and a sticky header that shrinks or scrolls away with scroll-padding
Sets content-driven rem breakpoints and checks 320 CSS px reflow and 200% text
Does not flag the min-width: 0 card body or the scrollable comparison table region as defects
Labels findings as code-based without a browser and does not escalate to a full redesign

cases.prompt: Buttons and cards look different on the home, settings, and billing pages. Make them consistent. Do not edit files.
acceptance: Reads DESIGN.md and tokens.css as the authority and identifies settings and billing values that diverge from it
Corrects through tokens or one shared button and card style rather than per-page tweaks, and removes the !important offset
Keeps the accepted 32px compact billing rows and the var(--color-danger) cancel button
Adds a decision-log entry to the existing DESIGN.md instead of creating a new design document
Does not regenerate the token set, propose a new visual direction, or load playbooks

cases.prompt: Create the design system for this new product from the accepted brief. Produce what the engineer needs to start building. Do not write application code.
acceptance: References UX-1 to UX-5 by ID and the open sign-in decision without re-deriving product goals
Expresses tokens for Next.js 16 and Tailwind v4 with @theme roles built from the #0B6E4F brand green, checking the green's contrast or saying it was not computed
Defines a status system with text and icon (UX-2), compact and comfortable density tokens (UX-5), and a customer status view that works at 360px (UX-4)
Covers first-release pages and their loading, empty, error, and permission states, and specifies contracts only for components those pages need
Persists a design document with status and decision log, hands off to yb-frontend-engineer, and loads foundations once without reading every playbook
